templates.name: Home Safety / Fall Risk Assessment
templates.description: At JOOLIE HEALTHCARE SERVICES, LLC., we understand that experiencing a fall can be a life-changing event That’s why we’ve developed our “Focus on fall prevention” program, a unique approach that pairs our clinical expertise with patient education for our patient and family to reduce fall risk by helping to address common causes of falls among our patients, including environmental hazards both inside and outside the home. This Home Safety Checklist will guide you through key environmental considerations to help and increase home safety and reduce the likelihood of falls in your homes or that of a loved one.

sections.title: Bathroom
sections.description: Check “YES” or “NO” for each item. Any No answers indicate a potential need for changes to the environment Exception: for questions marked “Yes = hazard”, a Yes answer indicates the hazard.

items.questionText: Is the path from the bedroom to the bathroom well lit?
Are there grab bars near the toilet and in the shower and bathtub?
If you have difficulty standing in the shower, do you use a shower seat?
Do your bathmats have slip-resistant backing?
Do you remove soap build-up in your shower/bathtub to avoid slipping?
Can you reach soap in the shower without bending down or turning too far around?
Do you have a raised toilet seat if you have difficulty standing up and sitting down?
Are spills cleaned up immediately?
Is there a table close to your bed with a lamp and room to store eye glasses and a phone?
Are cords pushed back against the wall?
Is there clutter on the floor?
Do you have a motion sensor night light?
Are throw rugs/floor mats secure?
Can you get to regularly used items without bending down or reaching up too far?
Are spills cleaned up immediately?
Is food prepared in the kitchen?
Are floor coverings secured and tidy?
Can you answer the phone without getting up?
Can you turn on a light without having to walk into a dark room?
Do you have a step stool that has side rails, sturdy and in good condition?
Do you have a cordless or cellular phone or an emergency alarm device?
Is it easy to walk around the furniture in your home?
Can you pull cords to lights or ceiling fans without reaching up?
Are there handrails on both sides of the stairways in your home?
Are the steps on your stairways even and safe?
Are there lights at the top and the bottom of the stairs?
Is the path from the house to the garage well lit?
Are there cracks or buckles on the sidewalks or driveway?
Are there hoses, weeds or other obstacles on the walkways?
Is there ice on steps or walkways?
